title: What does a 1:N model of a cargo UAV tell you about the 1:1 aircraft?
lede: research programme (proposal stage): per-quantity error budget for a Froude-scaled cargo aircraft model, with a stdlib scaling calculator; first-order result: at 1:10 the model needs 17 to 35% more power than Froude scaling predicts
summary: An open research programme on sub-scale flight testing of cargo and delivery aircraft. Dynamic (Froude) scaling keeps trim, mode frequencies and gust response, but Reynolds number falls as n<sup>1.5</sup>, so skin friction rises, and cell, motor and propeller performance do not scale with the airframe. The programme asks how large each error is for 1:2 to 1:20 models of an electric cargo aircraft, and whether a corrected model can recover it. Milestone 1 is a stdlib calculator (9 tests; exponent table dimensionally checked, ISA and Sutherland values checked) and a first-order flat-plate result for a 1,000 kg, aspect-ratio-10 airframe: at 1:10 the model needs 1.27× the Froude-scaled power (1.17 to 1.35 across form-factor, wetted-area and aspect-ratio sweeps) and L/D falls from 22.8 to 18.0. An untripped laminar-flow variant makes small models look better than full size, which is a modelling artefact and the reason the next milestones use XFOIL polars measured against UIUC data. The airframe constants are design choices, not a specific aircraft; the Froude exponents and the NASA TP-1435 and other citations are from memory and were not machine-checked (registries returned 403). Preliminary.
